In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the weak top-cycle is the most computationally tractable, followed by the strong top-cycle, and the rational top-cycle is the least tractable.
, in the presence of ties, the rational top-cycle is the most difficult choice set to compute.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the context of incomplete and tentative preferences, we provide a full picture of the possible and necessary winners for the weak, strong and rational top-cycles.
the weak and strong cycles are more robust against incompleteness than the rational cycle, but they are less expressive than the latter.
we have developed a complete theory for finding the necessary winners and possible winners for the three choice sets, with the only exception of the rational top-cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the necessary winner sets for the top-cycles are not affected by tentative incompleteness, whereas their possible winners are.

the rational top-cycle is the most robust choice set among the top-cycles in terms of the possible and necessary winners, which are always non-empty, whereas the weak and strong cycles can have empty sets of possible and necessary winners.
the weak and strong cycles, although not necessarily identical, have a common set of possible winners, while the rational top-cycle has a common set of necessary winners.
